claim: MF59 has been administered to more than 100 million people in more than 30 countries, in both seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines.
source: The squalene-based oil-in-water emulsion (SE) vaccine adjuvant MF59 has been administered to more than 100 million people in more than 30 countries, in both seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a factual claim about MF59's clinical use.

claim: Immunization of mice with MF59 or AddaVax plus soluble antigen results in robust antigen-specific antibody responses in lymph nodes and non-lymphoid tissues.
source: In this study we demonstrate that immunization of mice with MF59 or its mimetic AddaVax (AV) plus soluble antigen results in robust antigen-specific antibody and CD8 T cell responses in lymph nodes and non-lymphoid tissues.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Immunization of mice with MF59 or AddaVax plus soluble antigen results in robust antigen-specific CD8 T cell responses in lymph nodes and non-lymphoid tissues.
source: In this study we demonstrate that immunization of mice with MF59 or its mimetic AddaVax (AV) plus soluble antigen results in robust antigen-specific antibody and CD8 T cell responses in lymph nodes and non-lymphoid tissues.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Immunization with MF59 or AddaVax triggered rapid RIPK3-kinase dependent necroptosis in the lymph node which peaked at 6 hr.
source: Immunization triggered rapid RIPK3-kinase dependent necroptosis in the lymph node which peaked at 6 hr, followed by a sequential wave of apoptosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data in Figure 4.

claim: Immunization with MF59 or AddaVax was followed by a sequential wave of apoptosis after necroptosis.
source: Immunization triggered rapid RIPK3-kinase dependent necroptosis in the lymph node which peaked at 6 hr, followed by a sequential wave of apoptosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by western blot data showing cleaved caspase 3 in Figure 4.

claim: Immunization with alum plus antigen did not induce RIPK3-dependent signaling.
source: Immunization with alum plus antigen did not induce RIPK3-dependent signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by western blot data in Figure 4B showing no p-MLKL in alum-immunized mice.

claim: RIPK3-dependent signaling induced by MF59 or AddaVax was essential for cross-presentation of antigen to CD8 T cells by Batf3-dependent CD8+ DCs.
source: RIPK3-dependent signaling induced by MF59 or AV was essential for cross-presentation of antigen to CD8 T cells by Batf3-dependent CD8+ DCs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5 and 6 showing impaired CD8 T cell responses in RIPK3 KO and Batf3 KO mice.

claim: RIPK3 deficient mice were impaired in their ability to mount adjuvant-enhanced CD8 T cell responses.
source: Consistent with this, RIPK3 deficient or Batf3 deficient mice were impaired in their ability to mount adjuvant-enhanced CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6B showing reduced CD8 T cell responses in RIPK3 KO mice.

claim: Batf3 deficient mice were impaired in their ability to mount adjuvant-enhanced CD8 T cell responses.
source: Consistent with this, RIPK3 deficient or Batf3 deficient mice were impaired in their ability to mount adjuvant-enhanced CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 5D showing reduced CD8 T cell responses in Batf3 KO mice.

claim: CD8 T cell responses were unaffected in mice deficient in MLKL.
source: However, CD8 T cell responses were unaffected in mice deficient in MLKL, a downstream mediator of necroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6D showing normal CD8 T cell responses in MLKL KO mice.

claim: Antibody responses were unaffected in RIPK3-kinase deficient mice.
source: Surprisingly, antibody responses were unaffected in RIPK3-kinase or Batf3 deficient mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7C showing normal IgG responses in RIPK3 KO mice.

claim: Antibody responses were unaffected in Batf3 deficient mice.
source: Surprisingly, antibody responses were unaffected in RIPK3-kinase or Batf3 deficient mice.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B showing normal IgG responses in Batf3 KO mice.

claim: Antibody responses were impaired by in vivo administration of the pan-caspase inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK.
source: In contrast, antibody responses were impaired by in vivo administration of the pan-caspase inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK, but normal in caspase-1 deficient mice, suggesting a contribution from apoptotic caspases, in the induction of antibody responses.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7B showing reduced IgG responses with z-VAD-fmk treatment.

claim: Antibody responses were normal in caspase-1 deficient mice.
source: In contrast, antibody responses were impaired by in vivo administration of the pan-caspase inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK, but normal in caspase-1 deficient mice, suggesting a contribution from apoptotic caspases, in the induction of antibody responses.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C showing normal IgG responses in Caspase 1 KO mice.

claim: Squalene emulsion-based vaccine adjuvants induce antigen-specific CD8 T cell responses through RIPK3-dependent pathways.
source: These results demonstrate that squalene emulsion-based vaccine adjuvants induce antigen-specific CD8 T cell and antibody responses, through RIPK3-dependent and-independent pathways, respectively.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Squalene emulsion-based vaccine adjuvants induce antigen-specific antibody responses through RIPK3-independent pathways.
source: These results demonstrate that squalene emulsion-based vaccine adjuvants induce antigen-specific CD8 T cell and antibody responses, through RIPK3-dependent and-independent pathways, respectively.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The titers of Ova-specific IgG1 were comparable between the alum and SE groups.
source: The titers of Ova-specific IgG1 were comparable between the alum and SE groups, while titers of IgG2b and IgG2c (representing TH1 IgG response) were significantly elevated in SE groups (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Titers of IgG2b and IgG2c were significantly elevated in SE groups compared to alum.
source: The titers of Ova-specific IgG1 were comparable between the alum and SE groups, while titers of IgG2b and IgG2c (representing TH1 IgG response) were significantly elevated in SE groups (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The frequency of IFN-γ-producing OVA-specific CD4 T (TH1) cells was increased in AV group.
source: Consistent with this observation, the frequency of IFN-γ-producing OVA-specific CD4 T (TH1) cells was increased in AV group (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The generation of follicular helper T cells (TFH) was enhanced in SE groups.
source: Moreover, the generation of follicular helper T cells (TFH) was also enhanced in SE groups (Figure 1C), consistent with a higher frequency of germinal center (GC) B cells (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1C.

claim: SE groups showed a higher frequency of germinal center (GC) B cells.
source: Moreover, the generation of follicular helper T cells (TFH) was also enhanced in SE groups (Figure 1C), consistent with a higher frequency of germinal center (GC) B cells (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D and E.

claim: SE adjuvants elicit stronger IgG2b and IgG2c responses by potentiating helper TH1 and TFH cell activity and GC formation.
source: These data suggest that SE adjuvants elicit stronger IgG2b and IgG2c responses by potentiating helper TH1 and TFH cell activity and GC formation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Ova-specific CD8 T cell response in the AV group was significantly higher than in the alum group at day 7 post-boost.
source: In addition to antibody production, Ova-specific CD8 T cell response in the AV group was significantly higher than in the alum group at day 7 post-boost (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 1F.

claim: AV-induced Ova-specific CD8 T cells displayed enhanced expression of granzyme B.
source: Moreover, AV-induced Ova-specific CD8 T cells displayed enhanced expression of granzyme B, a surrogate indicator of cytotoxic function (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1G.

claim: Ova-specific CD8 T cells in the SE groups could be found systemically in non-lymphoid organs, but did not accumulate in the gut.
source: Notably, Ova-specific CD8 T cells in the SE groups could be found systemically in non-lymphoid organs, but did not accumulate in the gut (Figure 1H,I and J).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1H, I and J.

claim: Mice vaccinated with Ova+AV were fully protected from tumor challenge with Ova-expressing B16 melanoma.
source: Using this system, mice vaccinated with Ova+AV were fully protected from tumor challenge, while Ova+PBS vaccinated mice were not (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tumor growth and survival data in Figure 1K.

claim: Ova+PBS vaccinated mice were not protected from tumor challenge with Ova-expressing B16 melanoma.
source: Using this system, mice vaccinated with Ova+AV were fully protected from tumor challenge, while Ova+PBS vaccinated mice were not (Figure 1K).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tumor growth and survival data in Figure 1K.

claim: SE adjuvants can generate robust IgG responses and protective CD8 T cell responses.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that SE adjuvants can generate robust IgG responses and protective CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: SE groups displayed a significant increase of dLN size from 24 hr post-vaccination.
source: SE groups displayed a significant increase of dLN size from 24 hr post-vaccination, while no increase in cellularity could be detected in alum-immunized dLNs even at 48 hr (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by cell count data in Figure 2A.

claim: No increase in cellularity could be detected in alum-immunized dLNs even at 48 hr post-vaccination.
source: SE groups displayed a significant increase of dLN size from 24 hr post-vaccination, while no increase in cellularity could be detected in alum-immunized dLNs even at 48 hr (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by cell count data in Figure 2A.

claim: The increase of dLN cellularity was due to the rapid recruitment of monocytes and neutrophils, followed by late influx of DCs and lymphocytes including B and T cells.
source: The increase of dLN cellularity was due to the rapid recruitment of monocytes and neutrophils, followed by late influx of DCs and lymphocytes including B and T cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2B.

claim: Total LN cells in the SE groups showed higher Ag uptake when compared to LN cells from mock or alum groups.
source: Following vaccination, total LN cells in the SE groups showed higher Ag uptake when compared to LN cells from mock or alum groups (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data using Ova-AF647 in Figure 2C.

claim: Neutrophils, monocytes and DCs were mainly responsible for Ag uptake at early time points, but DCs dominated later on.
source: Neutrophils, monocytes and DCs were mainly responsible for Ag uptake at early time points, but DCs dominated later on (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2D.

claim: At 24 hr post-vaccination, migratory DCs (mDCs) and resident DCs (rDCs) in both AV and MF59 groups had significantly increased the expression of CD80 and CD86.
source: At 24 hr post-vaccination, migratory DCs (mDCs) and resident DCs (rDCs) in both AV and MF59 groups had significantly increased the expression of CD80 and CD86 (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D; Idoyaga et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2E.

claim: Kinetic analysis of CD80 expression on mDCs and rDCs showed a gradual increase in AV group over time.
source: Kinetic analysis of CD80 expression on mDCs and rDCs showed a gradual increase in AV group over time, while no significant alteration was detected in alum group until 48 hr post-vaccination (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2F.

claim: No significant alteration in CD80 expression was detected in alum group until 48 hr post-vaccination.
source: Kinetic analysis of CD80 expression on mDCs and rDCs showed a gradual increase in AV group over time, while no significant alteration was detected in alum group until 48 hr post-vaccination (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2F.

claim: SE adjuvants induce enhanced leukocyte recruitment, increased Ag uptake, and stronger DC activation.
source: Taken together, SE adjuvants induce enhanced leukocyte recruitment, increased Ag uptake, and stronger DC activation, potentially explaining the potency of subsequent adaptive immune responses (Calabro et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 2, with a citation to support the interpretation.

claim: SIGN-R1+ medullary macrophages within medullary inter-follicular regions are a primary collection point of lymph-borne antigen due to their proximal nature to the afferent lymphatics and high levels of phagocytosis.
source: Previous studies have established SIGN-R1+ medullary macrophages within medullary inter-follicular regions as a primary collection point of lymph-borne antigen due to their proximal nature to the afferent lymphatics and high levels of phagocytosis (Gray and Cyster, 2012; Woodruff et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to previous studies.

claim: At 2 hr post-immunization, lipophilic dye-labeled AV could be detected primarily within the medullary region of the dLN.
source: Indeed, at 2 hr post-immunization, lipophilic dye-labeled AV could be detected primarily within the medullary region of the dLN (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3A.

claim: Medullary cord macrophages (CD169- F4/80+, MCMs) and medullary sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80+, MSMs) were the most abundantly represented cell types (up to 50%) within the AV+ populations.
source: Flow cytometry analysis further verified that medullary cord macrophages (CD169- F4/80+, MCMs) and medullary sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80+, MSMs) were the most abundantly represented cell types (up to 50%) within the AV+ populations, although lower frequencies of other innate immune cells including neutrophils, monocytes, DCs and subcapsular sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80-, SSMs) were also AV+ (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B.

claim: Lower frequencies of neutrophils, monocytes, DCs and subcapsular sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80-, SSMs) were also AV+.
source: Flow cytometry analysis further verified that medullary cord macrophages (CD169- F4/80+, MCMs) and medullary sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80+, MSMs) were the most abundantly represented cell types (up to 50%) within the AV+ populations, although lower frequencies of other innate immune cells including neutrophils, monocytes, DCs and subcapsular sinus macrophages (CD169+ F4/80-, SSMs) were also AV+ (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B.

claim: At 24 hr after vaccination, dLNs in the AV and MF59 groups displayed a remarkable decrease of both MM and SSM populations with an almost complete loss of the subcapsular sinus lining.
source: At 24 hr after vaccination, PBS-injected dLNs displayed abundant MMs and a clear lining of SSMs along the subcapsular sinus. However, dLNs in the AV and MF59 groups displayed a remarkable decrease of both MM and SSM populations with an almost complete loss of the subcapsular sinus lining, while there were no such reductions in mice immunized with alum plus Ova (Figure 3C and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 3C and D.

claim: There were no reductions in MM and SSM populations in mice immunized with alum plus Ova.
source: At 24 hr after vaccination, PBS-injected dLNs displayed abundant MMs and a clear lining of SSMs along the subcapsular sinus. However, dLNs in the AV and MF59 groups displayed a remarkable decrease of both MM and SSM populations with an almost complete loss of the subcapsular sinus lining, while there were no such reductions in mice immunized with alum plus Ova (Figure 3C and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 3C and D.

claim: In the AV group at 4 hr and 12 hr post-vaccination, there was a striking reduction in the frequencies of both types of medullary macrophages (MCMs and MSMs).
source: However, in the AV group at 4 hr and 12 hr post-vaccination, there was a striking reduction in the frequencies of both types of medullary macrophages (MCMs and MSMs).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3E and F.

claim: There was a reduction in the frequencies of SSM in the AV group starting at 12 hr and dropping to the lowest levels at 48 hr.
source: Moreover, there was a reduction in the frequencies of SSM albeit with slower kinetics, starting at 12 hr and dropping to the lowest levels at 48 hr (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3E and F.

claim: MF59 caused a significant reduction of LN-resident macrophages at 24 hr post-immunization.
source: Similarly, MF59 also caused a significant reduction of LN-resident macrophages at 24 hr post-immunization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: MSMs displayed a significant and persistent reduction in absolute number after AV vaccination.
source: In terms of absolute number, MSMs displayed a significant and persistent reduction, while MCMs were reduced transiently and SSMs displayed a mild reduction (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3G.

claim: MCMs were reduced transiently in absolute number after AV vaccination.
source: In terms of absolute number, MSMs displayed a significant and persistent reduction, while MCMs were reduced transiently and SSMs displayed a mild reduction (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3G.

claim: SSMs displayed a mild reduction in absolute number after AV vaccination.
source: In terms of absolute number, MSMs displayed a significant and persistent reduction, while MCMs were reduced transiently and SSMs displayed a mild reduction (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3G.

claim: The efficient phagocytosis of SE adjuvants is associated with the early loss of MMs including MCMs and MSMs.
source: Collectively, these data show that the efficient phagocytosis of SE adjuvants is associated with the early loss of MMs including MCMs and MSMs, while the relatively slow accumulation of AV in SSMs is associated with the delayed and less pronounced loss.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The relatively slow accumulation of AV in SSMs is associated with the delayed and less pronounced loss.
source: Collectively, these data show that the efficient phagocytosis of SE adjuvants is associated with the early loss of MMs including MCMs and MSMs, while the relatively slow accumulation of AV in SSMs is associated with the delayed and less pronounced loss.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: AV induced dominant necrosis (AnnexinV- PI+) at early time points (up to 6 hr) in bone marrow-derived macrophages.
source: AV induced dynamic changes such as dominant necrosis (AnnexinV- PI+) at early time points (up to 6 hr), followed by delayed apoptosis (AnnexinV+ PI-) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4A.

claim: AV induced delayed apoptosis (AnnexinV+ PI-) in bone marrow-derived macrophages after early necrosis.
source: AV induced dynamic changes such as dominant necrosis (AnnexinV- PI+) at early time points (up to 6 hr), followed by delayed apoptosis (AnnexinV+ PI-) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4A.

claim: Phosphorylated-MLKL (p-MLKL) and cleaved caspase 1 were visible at 3 hr and strongly induced at 6 hr in AV-immunized dLNs.
source: Consistent with the in vitro cell death data, phosphorylated-MLKL (p-MLKL) and cleaved caspase 1 (markers of necroptosis and inflammasome activation/pyroptosis respectively) were visible at 3 hr, and were strongly induced at 6 hr in AV-immunized dLNs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4B.

claim: Immuno-fluorescent staining verified necroptosis signaling in the medullar following AV immunization.
source: Immuno-fluorescent staining of phosphorylated RIPK3 and MLKL verified necroptosis signaling in the medullar following AV immunization (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4C.

claim: Induction of MLKL phosphorylation was confirmed to be RIPK3-dependent as no positive p-MLKL signal could be observed within AV-immunized RIPK3-KO animals.
source: Induction of MLKL phosphorylation was confirmed to be RIPK3-dependent as no positive p-MLKL signal could be observed within AV-immunized RIPK3-KO animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No MLKL phosphorylation and lower levels of cleaved caspase 1 were detected in alum-immunized dLNs.
source: Meanwhile no MLKL phosphorylation and lower levels of cleaved caspase 1 were detected in alum-immunized dLNs.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4B.

claim: There was increased apoptosis in the dLNs of mice immunized with alum, as evidenced by enhanced cleavage of caspase 3 at 3 hr and 6 hr.
source: Furthermore, there was increased apoptosis in the dLNs of mice immunized with alum, as evidenced by enhanced cleavage of caspase 3 at 3 hr and 6 hr, while AV injection displayed a strong activation of caspase 3 at 24 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4B.

claim: AV injection displayed a strong activation of caspase 3 at 24 hr.
source: Furthermore, there was increased apoptosis in the dLNs of mice immunized with alum, as evidenced by enhanced cleavage of caspase 3 at 3 hr and 6 hr, while AV injection displayed a strong activation of caspase 3 at 24 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4B.

claim: MF59 vaccination induced similar cell death phenotypes in dLNs as AV.
source: These cell death phenotypes in dLNs were also true for MF59 vaccination (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: After SE-adjuvanted immunization, there is early regulated necrosis such as MLKL-mediated necroptosis and pyroptosis, followed by delayed apoptosis in dLNs.
source: Thus, although these data do not give information on which cell types are undergoing cell death, they suggest that after SE-adjuvanted immunization, there is early regulated necrosis such as MLKL-mediated necroptosis and pyroptosis, followed by delayed apoptosis in dLNs.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Subcutaneous injection of CLL resulted in efficient depletion of MSM and SSM subsets in dLNs.
source: Consistent with the literature, subcutaneous injection of CLL resulted in efficient depletion of MSM and SSM subsets in dLNs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Following macrophage depletion by CLL, Ova+AV vaccination resulted in significantly decreased MLKL phosphorylation and altered kinetics of caspase1 cleavage.
source: Interestingly, following macrophage depletion, Ova+AV vaccination resulted in significantly decreased MLKL phosphorylation and altered kinetics of caspase1 cleavage (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by western blot data in Figure 4D.

claim: LN-resident macrophages contribute substantially to the observed necroptosis in dLNs after AV vaccination.
source: These data, combined with the observed loss of the LN-resident macrophage populations by both flow cytometry and immunofluorescence (Figure 3C–G) suggests that LN-resident macrophages contribute substantially to the observed necroptosis in dLNs after AV vaccination.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: MMs displaying cleaved caspase 3 were detected after the AV vaccination.
source: In addition to putative LN-resident macrophages undergoing necroptosis, MMs displaying cleaved caspase 3 were also detected after the AV vaccination (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4E.

claim: Necrotic cells, including necrotic monocytes/macrophages and a necrotic macrophage were observed predominantly at the medulla of dLNs after 1 hr of AV injection.
source: In contrast to the minimal level of dying cells in dLNs of naïve mice, necrotic cells (red arrows), including necrotic monocytes/macrophages (1 hr) and a necrotic macrophage (4 hr) were observed predominantly at the medulla of dLNs after 1 hr of AV injection (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 4F.

claim: LN-resident macrophages undergo early necrosis and delayed apoptosis upon AV immunization.
source: Together these data consistently support the idea that LN-resident macrophages undergo early necrosis and delayed apoptosis upon AV immunization.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Cytokines such as IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12 and TNF were released into serum by AV vaccination.
source: Indeed, cytokines such as IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12 and TNF were released into serum by AV vaccination (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 4G.

claim: IL-6, IL-12 and TNF were particularly elevated by AV vaccination in comparison with the alum group.
source: IL-6, IL-12 and TNF were particularly elevated by AV vaccination in comparison with the alum group.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 4G.

claim: Elevated levels of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and uric acid could be increasingly detected in serum of AV-immunized mice at 24 hr.
source: Moreover, elevated levels of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) and uric acid, well described DAMPs could be increasingly detected in serum of AV-immunized mice at 24 hr (Figure 4H; Ko et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by DAMP detection assays in Figure 4H.

claim: The subcutaneous injection of SE adjuvants can induce mixed types of cell death signaling pathways which in turn set up a highly immuno-stimulatory microenvironment.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that the subcutaneous injection of SE adjuvants can induce mixed types of cell death signaling pathways which in turn set up a highly immuno-stimulatory microenvironment.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Following macrophage depletion by CLL treatment, Ova+AV vaccination resulted in reduced activation of the mDC subset, compared to control liposome treatment at 24 hr.
source: Following macrophage depletion by CLL treatment, Ova+AV vaccination resulted in reduced activation of the mDC subset, compared to control liposome treatment at 24 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Production of IL-6 was dramatically attenuated following macrophage depletion by CLL treatment.
source: Production of IL-6 was also dramatically attenuated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Ova-specific CD8 T cell responses were significantly decreased in the CLL-treated group at day 7 post-boost.
source: Importantly, Ova-specific CD8 T cell responses were significantly decreased in the CLL-treated group at day 7 post-boost (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 5A.

claim: Upon intraperitoneal DT injection, CD169-DTR mice showed efficient depletion in MSM and SSM subsets.
source: Upon intraperitoneal DT injection, CD169-DTR mice showed efficient depletion in MSM and SSM subsets, while LysM-iDTR mice displayed only SSM depletion (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C; Gupta et al., 2016; Shaabani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5B.

claim: LysM-iDTR mice displayed only SSM depletion upon intraperitoneal DT injection.
source: Upon intraperitoneal DT injection, CD169-DTR mice showed efficient depletion in MSM and SSM subsets, while LysM-iDTR mice displayed only SSM depletion (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C; Gupta et al., 2016; Shaabani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CD8 T cell responses were normal in the LysM-iDTR group.
source: Surprisingly, in contrast to normal CD8 T cell responses in the LysM-iDTR group (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), the CD169-DTR group showed significant reduction of CD8 T cell responses in spleen and lung (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The CD169-DTR group showed significant reduction of CD8 T cell responses in spleen and lung.
source: Surprisingly, in contrast to normal CD8 T cell responses in the LysM-iDTR group (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), the CD169-DTR group showed significant reduction of CD8 T cell responses in spleen and lung (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 5C.

claim: LN-resident macrophages are required for the efficient activation of innate immune response and the optimal induction of CD8 T cell response by SE adjuvants.
source: These data demonstrate that LN macrophages are required for the efficient activation of innate immune response and the optimal induction of CD8 T cell response by SE adjuvants.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: CD8a+ DCs are the key mediators of antigen cross-presentation to CD8 T cells.
source: With respect to the cell types involved in Ag cross-presentation to CD8 T cells, it is known that CD8a+ DCs are the key mediators of this process (den Haan et al., 2000; Hildner et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to previous studies.

claim: Batf3+ DCs such as Xcr1+ CD103+ DCs are essential for cross-presentation of skin-derived Ags to CD8 T cells.
source: It has been reported that Batf3+ DCs such as Xcr1+ CD103+ DCs essential for cross-presentation of skin-derived Ags to CD8 T cells (Bedoui et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to a previous study.

claim: CD169+ macrophages are capable of Ag cross-presentation to CD8 T cells without DCs in specific experimental settings.
source: In contrast, a recent study suggested that CD169+ macrophages are capable of Ag cross-presentation to CD8 T cells without DCs in specific experimental settings (Bernhard et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to a previous study.

claim: In the absence of Batf3+ DC populations, the Ova-specific CD8 T cell response was substantially impaired.
source: In the absence of Batf3+ DC populations (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), the Ova-specific CD8 T cell response was substantially impaired (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 5D.

claim: Cross-presentation by Batf3+ DCs is critical for the generation of CD8 T cell responses in SE-adjuvanted vaccination.
source: This implies that cross-presentation by Batf3+ DCs is critical for the generation of CD8 T cell responses in SE-adjuvanted vaccination.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 5D.

claim: LN macrophages and Batf3-dependent CD103+ DCs are necessary for optimal induction of antigen-specific CD8 T cell response to SE adjuvants.
source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that LN macrophages and Batf3-dependent CD103+ DCs are necessary for optimal induction of antigen-specific CD8 T cell response to SE adjuvants.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 5.

claim: Neither individual TLR deficiency (TLR3, TLR4, TLR7, and TLR9) nor the absence of adaptor proteins such as MyD88 and TRIF affected AV-induced CD8 T cell response.
source: Surprisingly, neither individual TLR deficiency (TLR3, TLR4, TLR7, and TLR9) nor the absence of adaptor proteins such as MyD88 and TRIF affected AV-induced CD8 T cell response. (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The CD8 T cell response was normal in ASC KO and Caspase 1 KO mice.
source: To probe the role of inflammasomes and pyroptosis, we examined the CD8 T cell response in ASC KO and Caspase 1 KO mice and observed that the CD8 T cell response was normal in these mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In vivo inhibition of pan-caspase activity by z-VAD-fmk did not influence the normal CD8 T cell response.
source: In addition, in vivo inhibition of pan-caspase activity by z-VAD-fmk did not influence the normal CD8 T cell response (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that neither inflammasome activation/pyroptosis nor apoptosis is crucial for AV-induced CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Neither inflammasome activation/pyroptosis nor apoptosis is crucial for AV-induced CD8 T cell responses.
source: In addition, in vivo inhibition of pan-caspase activity by z-VAD-fmk did not influence the normal CD8 T cell response (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that neither inflammasome activation/pyroptosis nor apoptosis is crucial for AV-induced CD8 T cell responses.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: An injection of necroptotic cells rather than apoptotic cells generated potent CD8 T cell response.
source: A previous report by Yatim et al. demonstrated that an injection of necroptotic cells rather than apoptotic cells generated potent CD8 T cell response (Yatim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to a previous study.

claim: At 24 hr after vaccination, RIPK3 KO mice displayed significantly impaired secretion of IL-6 and TNF in serum.
source: At 24 hr after vaccination, RIPK3 KO mice displayed significantly impaired secretion of IL-6 and TNF in serum (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 6A.

claim: In the absence of RIPK3, CD8 T cell response in various tissues was significantly reduced by AV vaccination, as compared to WT mice.
source: Remarkably, in the absence of RIPK3, CD8 T cell response in various tissues was significantly reduced by AV vaccination, as compared to WT mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6B.

claim: Vaccination with MF59 in RIPK3 KO mice resulted in a significant decrease of CD8 T cells.
source: Consistent with AV data, vaccination with MF59 in RIPK3 KO mice resulted in a significant decrease of CD8 T cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The kinase activity of RIPK3 was critical for SE adjuvant-mediated CD8 T cell response since RIPK3 kinase-dead (RIPK3 K51A) mice abrogated the response.
source: We demonstrate that the kinase activity of RIPK3 was critical for SE adjuvant-mediated CD8 T cell response since RIPK3 kinase-dead (RIPK3 K51A) mice abrogated the response.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6C.

claim: RIPK3 K51A mice were significantly impaired in their capacity to induce Ova-specific CD8 T cell responses in multiple tissues, albeit to a lesser degree than RIPK3 KO mice.
source: RIPK3 K51A mice were also significantly impaired in their capacity to induce Ova-specific CD8 T cell responses in multiple tissues, albeit to a lesser degree than RIPK3 KO mice (Figure 6C), suggesting that the kinase-dependent activity of RIPK3 is necessary for induction of CD8 T cell response by SE adjuvants.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6C.

claim: The kinase-dependent activity of RIPK3 is necessary for induction of CD8 T cell response by SE adjuvants.
source: RIPK3 K51A mice were also significantly impaired in their capacity to induce Ova-specific CD8 T cell responses in multiple tissues, albeit to a lesser degree than RIPK3 KO mice (Figure 6C), suggesting that the kinase-dependent activity of RIPK3 is necessary for induction of CD8 T cell response by SE adjuvants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6C.

claim: Deficiency of MLKL did not affect Ova-specific CD8 T cell response after Ova+AV vaccination.
source: Notably, deficiency of MLKL, an effector molecule of necroptosis, did not affect Ova-specific CD8 T cell response after Ova+AV vaccination (Figure 6D), implying an alternate pathway for RIPK3 function in this system outside of the classically described execution of necroptosis.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by tetramer staining data in Figure 6D.

claim: There is an alternate pathway for RIPK3 function in this system outside of the classically described execution of necroptosis.
source: Notably, deficiency of MLKL, an effector molecule of necroptosis, did not affect Ova-specific CD8 T cell response after Ova+AV vaccination (Figure 6D), implying an alternate pathway for RIPK3 function in this system outside of the classically described execution of necroptosis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6D.

claim: BMMs from the RIPK3 KO mouse resulted in the significantly decreased proliferation of OT-I cells compared to WT BMMs.
source: Strikingly, BMMs from the RIPK3 KO mouse resulted in the significantly decreased proliferation of OT-I cells, as compared to WT BMMs (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by in vitro cross-presentation assay data in Figure 6E.

claim: RIPK3-dependent signaling in dLN-resident macrophages is necessary for optimal CD8 T cell responses to SE-adjuvanted immunization.
source: Therefore, these data demonstrate that RIPK3-dependent signaling in dLN-resident macrophages is necessary for optimal CD8 T cell responses to SE-adjuvanted immunization.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The depletion of both SSM and MSM in CD169-DTR mice resulted in the significant reduction of Ova-specific IgG responses.
source: Consistent with the role of macrophages in CD8 T cell responses, the depletion of both SSM and MSM in CD169-DTR mice resulted in the significant reduction of Ova-specific IgG responses (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7A.

claim: There were normal IgG responses in CLL-treated mice.
source: In contrast, there were normal IgG responses in CLL-treated mice and LysM-iDTR mice (Data not shown and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: There were normal IgG responses in LysM-iDTR mice.
source: In contrast, there were normal IgG responses in CLL-treated mice and LysM-iDTR mice (Data not shown and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The absence of Batf3+ DCs did not alter IgG responses.
source: Furthermore, the absence of Batf3+ DCs did not alter IgG responses (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In vivo treatment with the pan-caspase inhibitor, z-VAD-fmk, resulted in a profound decrease in antigen-specific IgG1 titers induced by AV.
source: In contrast to the CD8 T cell response, in vivo treatment with the pan-caspase inhibitor, z-VAD-fmk, resulted in a profound decrease in antigen-specific IgG1 titers induced by AV (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7B.

claim: The inhibition of RIPK1 by Nec-1s injection had no effect on IgG responses in AV vaccination.
source: However, the inhibition of RIPK1 by Nec-1s injection or RIPK3 deficiency had no effect on IgG responses in AV vaccination (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7B.

claim: RIPK3 deficiency had no effect on IgG responses in AV vaccination.
source: However, the inhibition of RIPK1 by Nec-1s injection or RIPK3 deficiency had no effect on IgG responses in AV vaccination (Figure 7B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7C.

claim: Impaired inflammasome formation in ASC KO and caspase 1 KO mice resulted in normal IgG responses.
source: In addition, impaired inflammasome formation in ASC KO and caspase 1 KO mice resulted in normal IgG responses (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Caspase-dependent apoptosis, rather than a RIPK3-dependent pathway might be primarily important for antibody responses induced by AV vaccination.
source: This suggests that caspase-dependent apoptosis, rather than a RIPK3-dependent pathway might be primarily important for antibody responses induced by AV vaccination.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Figure 7B and C.

claim: The efficient generation of IgG responses was associated with the release of dsDNA since the co-injection of DNaseI significantly decreased the IgG responses by AV.
source: In the AV-adjuvanted vaccination model, the efficient generation of IgG responses was also associated with the release of dsDNA since the co-injection of DNaseI significantly decreased the IgG responses by AV (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7D.

claim: The MyD88 pathway was required for the generation of optimal IgG responses by SE adjuvant.
source: In alignments with a previous report (Seubert et al., 2011), the MyD88 pathway was required for the generation of optimal IgG responses by SE adjuvant although some of individual TLRs are moderately associated (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: Some individual TLRs are moderately associated with IgG responses by SE adjuvant.
source: In alignments with a previous report (Seubert et al., 2011), the MyD88 pathway was required for the generation of optimal IgG responses by SE adjuvant although some of individual TLRs are moderately associated (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by ELISA data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: The caspase activity in macrophages and subsequent release of DAMPs might play important roles in the SE adjuvant-mediated IgG responses.
source: Altogether, these data suggest that the caspase activity in macrophages and subsequent release of DAMPs might play important roles in the SE adjuvant-mediated IgG responses.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Induction of antigen-specific CD8 T cell responses in mice immunized with MF59 or its mimetic AV occurs through a mechanism dependent on RIPK3 signaling in LN macrophages.
source: In this study, we present evidence that induction of antigen-specific CD8 T cell responses in mice immunized with MF59 or its mimetic AV occurs through a mechanism dependent on RIPK3 signaling in LN macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main finding in the Discussion section.

claim: SE adjuvants are primarily acquired by LN-resident macrophages, resulting in their elimination through various cell death pathways including apoptosis and regulated necrosis.
source: Using several independent models, we demonstrate that the SE adjuvants are primarily acquired by LN-resident macrophages, resulting in their elimination through various cell death pathways including apoptosis and regulated necrosis.
evidence: This is a summary statement of findings in the Discussion section.

claim: Staphylococcus aureus infection, Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA) vaccination or the saponin based adjuvant caused the disruption of SSM layer in dLNs.
source: These infection/vaccination-mediated damage response doesn't seem to be rare event because recent studies have demonstrated that Staphylococcus aureus infection, Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA) vaccination or the saponin based adjuvant caused the disruption of SSM layer in dLNs, which in turn significantly modulate subsequent B cell or T cell responses, respectively (Detienne et al., 2016; Gaya et al., 2015; Sagoo et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to previous studies.

claim: The MSM subset, rather than SSMs, is critical for the uptake of the SE adjuvant, inducing cell death-associated signaling, and ultimately required for optimal adaptive immune responses.
source: In this SE adjuvant vaccination model, it is worth noting that the MSM subset, rather than SSMs, is critical for the uptake of the SE adjuvant, inducing cell death-associated signaling, and ultimately required for optimal adaptive immune responses.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: The induction of optimal antigen-specific antibody responses by SE adjuvants is associated with caspase activity and dsDNA release.
source: Importantly, we demonstrate the induction of optimal antigen-specific antibody responses by SE adjuvants is associated with caspase activity and dsDNA release (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: RIPK3-dependent signaling is critical for optimal CD8 T cell response, but was not necessary for IgG responses.
source: Thus, while RIPK3-dependent signaling is critical for optimal CD8 T cell response, it was not necessary for IgG responses.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion section.

claim: RIPK3 is essential in the induction of MLKL-dependent necroptosis.
source: RIPK3 is known to be essential in the induction of MLKL-dependent necroptosis, but recent studies have established additional roles for RIPK3 in kinase-dependent cytokine induction and kinase-independent scaffolding function (Kang et al., 2013; Lawlor et al., 2015; Muendlein et al., 2020; Najjar et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to previous studies.

claim: Recent studies have established additional roles for RIPK3 in kinase-dependent cytokine induction and kinase-independent scaffolding function.
source: RIPK3 is known to be essential in the induction of MLKL-dependent necroptosis, but recent studies have established additional roles for RIPK3 in kinase-dependent cytokine induction and kinase-independent scaffolding function (Kang et al., 2013; Lawlor et al., 2015; Muendlein et al., 2020; Najjar et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to previous studies.

claim: The kinase activity of RIPK3 was critical for SE adjuvant-mediated CD8 T cell response.
source: We demonstrate that the kinase activity of RIPK3 was critical for SE adjuvant-mediated CD8 T cell response since RIPK3 kinase-dead (RIPK3 K51A) mice abrogated the response.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: The execution step of necroptosis is dispensable in eliciting CD8 T cell response although RIPK3's kinase activity is still required.
source: Further investigation using MLKL-deficient mice has revealed the dispensability of the execution step of necroptosis in eliciting CD8 T cell response although RIPK3's kinase activity is still required.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 6D.

claim: The increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines by RIPK3-associated signaling is essential for the optimal CD8 T cell response to SE-adjuvanted immunization.
source: Thus we propose that the increased secretion of proinflammatory cytokines by RIPK3-associated signaling is essential for the optimal CD8 T cell response to SE-adjuvanted immunization (Snyder et al., 2019; Yatim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism stated in the Discussion with citations to support the interpretation.

claim: Caspase activity is necessary for the efficient induction of IgG response by SE adjuvants.
source: In contrast, our data suggest that caspase activity is necessary for the efficient induction of IgG response by SE adjuvants.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 7B.

claim: The SE-adjuvanted immunization establishes a highly immuno-stimulatory environment.
source: Our data also demonstrate that the SE-adjuvanted immunization establishes a highly immuno-stimulatory environment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Increased secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and DAMPs such as IL-6, IL-12 and TNF, and dsDNA was observed by the SE adjuvant.
source: We observed increased secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines and DAMPs such as IL-6, IL-12 and TNF, and dsDNA by the SE adjuvant.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 4G and H.

claim: The release of pro-inflammatory mediators provides a feed-forward mechanism in the further elimination of macrophages and the efficient activation of DCs.
source: It is possible that the release of pro-inflammatory mediators provides a feed-forward mechanism in the further elimination of macrophages and the efficient activation of DCs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement in the Discussion section.

claim: The CD8 T cell response by MF59 and its analog AV can be triggered via RIPK3-dependent signaling in dLN macrophages, whilst antibody responses occur independently of this pathway.
source: In conclusion, our results demonstrate that the CD8 T cell response, by MF59 and its analog AV, can be triggered via RIPK3-dependent signaling in dLN macrophages, whilst antibody responses occur independently of this pathway.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Pharmacological or genetic manipulation of these pathways may provide novel mediators of vaccine immunity.
source: These results suggest that pharmacological or genetic manipulation of these pathways may provide novel mediators of vaccine immunity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement in the Discussion section.
